newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai port to raise capacity to 220 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai port to raise capacity to 220 mln tonnes.

text.p: China is expanding its port at Shanghai with the goal of creating an international shipping centre, the Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.
The port plans to increase annual handling capacity to 220 million tonnes by the end of the century and to 280 million tonnes by 2010, it said.
Shanghai Port was expected to raise its container handling capacity from 1.9 million TEUs to at least 2.5 million TEUs by 2000 and more than six million by the year 2010, it said.

The city plans to invest more than 10 billion yuan (US$1.21 billion) on dredging the mouth of the Yangtze river within seven to 10 years to allow the most modern container ships to reach the port, Xinhua said.

If all goes according to plan, the port -- plagued by a serious sludge problem for half a century -- will become a flourishing international water transport centre, it quoted Xu Bozhang, an official in charge of construction of the international shipping centre, as saying.

Among Shanghai's advantages are that the industrial and trading hub handles $52 billion worth of goods each year, Xinhua quoted Cao Lansheng, director of the Planning and Development Commission of the China Port Association, as saying.
With economic growth in the Yangtze river delta averaging between 14 and 20 percent, the volume of container freight at the port is growing by 30 percent a year, Cao said.
The seven provinces along the Yangtze valley and the Shanghai municipality produce 40 percent of China's gross national produce and 21 percent of total trade, Xinhua said.
Shanghai port handles one-quarter of China's sea cargo, it said.
